subject: Pricing and commit structure for multi-region hosted API
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@neotech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-05T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing and commit structure for multi-region hosted API

Hi Samira —

Great talking yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to lay out two commit options tailored to your usage profile and clarify how cross-region consumption would be billed:

1) Blended volume commit (simple):
- $0.0045 / 1k tokens baseline for up to 1B tokens / month across regions.
- Above 1B: step-down to $0.0038 / 1k tokens.
- Billing: single monthly invoice, usage aggregated across regions with a blended rate.

2) Regional buckets (control):
- You reserve separate commit buckets by region (US, EU, APAC). Each bucket has its own tiered pricing.
- APAC has a +12% location surcharge applied to the final per-token rate due to regional capacity costs.
- Unused commit in one bucket cannot be automatically reallocated unless you add the optional spill policy.

A few clarifying notes:
- Egress/storage/embedding costs are already included in the baseline per-token price unless explicitly flagged in the SOW.
- If you want guaranteed latency SLAs for APAC production traffic, we recommend a dedicated APAC pool (adds a fixed monthly capacity fee).
- We can implement a spill policy so excess usage in one region draws from another bucket at a reconciled blended rate (useful to avoid overage spikes).

I've attached Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_v3.pdf and a starter Draft_SOW_Neotech.docx so your procurement team can review.

If you can share an anonymized month of regional token distribution (US/EU/APAC breakdown), I can run a cost model and recommend the lowest-risk commit mix.

Thanks — I can carve 30 minutes tomorrow for a quick walkthrough with Lauren on the regional details.

Best,
Karthik

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the write-up and the attachments — useful detail. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we share with procurement:

- When you say "aggregated across regions with a blended rate" in option 1, will the blended rate be calculated by actual regional usage that month (i.e., true blended), or by a pre-agreed weighting? We need to understand month-to-month volatility implications.
- For APAC surcharge: is that a fixed percentage or does it vary by instance type / dedicated vs. shared capacity?
- If we choose regional buckets, can we set a spill policy that triggers only when a regional bucket exceeds 110% of its commit? That reduces surprise charges for us.

Also, we anticipate a spike in APAC traffic for a pilot in late Q2 (roughly 200–250M tokens over 2 weeks). Can you confirm how burst capacity would work and whether the APAC surcharge applies to burst usage as well?

Looping in Alex from platform and procurement questions. Procurement will need the SOW and a clear statement of how cross-region billing appears on the invoice.

Best,
Samira
Head of Product | Neotech Solutions
samira.khan@neotech.com

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-06T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and commit structure for multi-region hosted API

Thanks Samira — quick answers inline and a proposed default we often recommend: 

- Blended calculation: we can do either. Default is true blended by actual monthly consumption (so your bill reflects where traffic actually happened). If you'd prefer a fixed weighting for budgeting, we can lock that in (requires an amendment).

- APAC surcharge: default is a fixed percentage (+12%) on shared capacity. If you go with a dedicated APAC pool for SLA, the surcharge is reduced to +6% because we reserve capacity and can optimize placement.

- Spill policy: yes — we can configure spill only after 110% consumption. Any spill usage will bill at the higher of (a) originating bucket's rate or (b) a reconciled blended rate depending on your preference. We document exact mechanics in the SOW.

- Burst capacity: we support on-demand burst up to 2x baseline for short windows; bursts draw from available shared pools by default and will inherit the same regional surcharge rules unless you pre-purchase burst credits (recommended for predictable pilots).

Proposed default for Neotech pilot: a blended global commit for baseline (reduces admin overhead) + a small dedicated APAC capacity slice to keep your pilot latency predictable. That combination tends to minimize unit cost while protecting critical APAC latency.

We're happy to model the Q2 pilot numbers — Karthik, can you ask Neotech for the expected regional split for that pilot?

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Alex Patel <alex.patel@neotech.com>

Date: 2026-03-07T02:18:00+08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and commit structure for multi-region hosted API

Thanks — procurement asked for a quick summary to include in the purchase request. A couple of contract items procurement will need clarified before we run this past finance: 

1) Invoicing visibility: we need line-item detail per region (US/EU/APAC) and an explanation of how blended maths show up if we pick option 1.
2) Credits & refunds: how are unused committed tokens handled at termination or renewal? We need a 90-day true-up window and pro-rata on termination.
3) Data residency: for EU traffic, we want assurance that EU tokens processed in EU nodes stay within the EU cluster unless failover occurs. How do you document that in the SOW?

I'll attach their checklist later today. For now please confirm (a) line-item invoices are available, (b) a 90-day true-up is acceptable, and (c) we can add explicit language about EU processing locality with failover language.

—Alex
Director, Platform Engineering | Neotech Solutions

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Patel <alex.patel@neotech.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@neotech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procure@neotech.com
Date: 2026-03-08T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing and commit structure for multi-region hosted API

Alex / Samira —

Appreciate the checklist. Short answers:

a) Line-item invoices: yes — we can provide monthly invoices with per-region usage rows, blended math footnotes, and a summary line that shows the final effective per-token rate.

b) True-up: a 90-day true-up window with pro-rata treatment on termination is acceptable; we'll put the exact formula in the SOW (standard practice).

c) EU processing locality: we will include a data residency clause that specifies EU traffic is routed to EU nodes by default and failover to non-EU nodes only occurs under documented emergency conditions; failover triggers and audit logs will be enumerated in the SOW.

Next steps: I will schedule a 30-minute call with Lauren and Marissa to walk procurement through the SOW and invoice examples. If procurement can share the pilot regional breakdown (even approximate), we'll produce a cost comparison (blended vs. regional buckets + dedicated APAC slice) by EOD Friday.

If that sounds good I'll send a calendar invite and a short one-page procurement summary.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to the next step.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
